I’ll tell ya one thing for sure coming from the area we “bred” these resistances to exist originally… herbicides aren’t the best option, it’s way too dang genetically diverse and therefore adaptable. Its consistent weaknesses are its inherent life cycles, and it is easier to control with cultural practices that make your field unappealing habitat. Palmer is a classic pioneer species and thrives in heavily disturbed (think tilled, dry, exposed to sun, etc) sites. The more soil coverage with residue, living mulch, literal mulch, and the less tilling you do the more it subsides even without herbicide control. Around here you rarely see a no-till or strip till field with amaranth pressure, while all the moldboard plow guys are absolutely slammed with it and spraying constantly eating up $$$. And that’s with 10-18” of rainfall annually, they are near invincible when they get some water.

When we were regularly using pre-plant incorporated herbicides, pigweed/water hemp was our most common escape weed.  So, it's not the answer without other techniques layered over or afterwards.  
Clean plowing once might help reset a terribly bad field, but if you continue tillage in future years, those seeds return to the germination depth.  A moldboard plowing helped us break an infestation of herbicide resistant lambsquarters in the '80s, when it was just getting worse with disks & field cultivator.
Plowing would not impact this problem, however, shallow tillage, either interrow, pre plant or post harvest (if the weed has not yet set seed) would absolutely help
